newsitem.title: USA: Dow industrials higher at midday, tech stocks soft.
newsitem.headline: Dow industrials higher at midday, tech stocks soft.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose Monday while technology stocks drifted as investors anxiously awaited a slew of economic reports due later this week.
Just after 1 p.m., the Dow Jones industrial average rose 33.91 points to 8,147.35, underpinned by strength in the bond market, where long-term interest rates fell.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a narrow 14-13 margin on moderate New York Stock Exchange volume of 253 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite added 0.91 points to 1,570.49.

"The market is drifting here," said Charles White, managing director of Avatar Associates. "There are a bunch of economic numbers coming out this week ... so investors are on the threshold, waiting for some more news to come out."

Blue-chip stocks set records for three straight sessions last week after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan painted a generally rosy picture of the economy and seemed to indicate the central bank was not ready to raise short-term interest rates soon.

But investors will be watching this week's economic data closely for confirmation that growth is moderating enough to keep the Fed from raising short-term rates in a bid to ward off inflation, analysts said.

The second-quarter employment cost index, due Tuesday, would be watched for any sign of a pickup in wage inflation, the analysts said. Later in the week, the government gives the first glimpse of the economy's overall performance in the second quarter, and the July jobs report is due Friday.
"We have some serious numbers coming out this week," said Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics.

"If it all adds up, the numbers could add credence to Greenspan's presentation," he said. "But if the employment cost index or the employment report are bad, it could be extremely disturbing to markets."
"Though we have been up most of the day, the market is a little skittish," said Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage.
"People are starting to wonder if the economy can get a whole lot better than it is now," he said. "Economic conditions have to stay exactly perfect for the market to stay at these kind of levels."

Stocks got a lift from the bond market, where the 30-year Treasury rose 14/32, or $4.38 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.42 percent from 6.46 percent Friday. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Technology stocks were mixed. Shares of personal computer makers fell after Bear Stearns analyst Andrew Neff downgraded Dell Computer Corp., voicing concerns over the stock's lofty price.
Dell fell 1-5/8 to 79-7/8, Compaq Computer lost 3-3/16 to 132-1/4 and International Business Machines slipped 14/16 to 106-1/16.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 2.15 points to 940.94.
The American Stock Exchange index added 1.10 points to 638.90.
